limitations: TOFU-style local child startup enrollment remains a trusted-process assumption: the root-signed keyset does NOT independently attest the PDP binary, process isolation, executable identity or a remotely authenticated server. Signing a key observed from a compromised local launch would still authorize that compromised key.
Offline governance root is generated in CI memory without HSM, PKI, secure key custody, independent multi-party issuance or production certificate authority.

Published keyset epochs, checkpoints and revoked tombstones live in one process: no independently anchored durable anti-rollback store, cross-instance propagation, partition consensus or reboot recovery.
The trust root itself is not rotated; trusted root replacement requires a separate independently approved cross-signing or secure provisioning protocol.
Fake injected clock supplies not-before/expiry checks; secure external time, CRL/OCSP equivalents, consistent revocation propagation and signed timestamps do not exist.
W2.6 Node child executes synthetic rules, not real approved cooperative policy or the W1 Python simulator.
Existing W2.4 file audit remains temporary; W2.5 version metadata and W2.7 keyset state are not persistently signed and anchored in an operational ledger.
No live shareholder, brokerage, trade approval, payment, database, financial accounting, official source admission, Next app route, Nest AppModule, RLS, Docker or production deployment.
